hero.title: Étretat Beach: cliffs, tides,
hero.description: Plan your Étretat visit with parking, tide information and views of Aval and Amont. Walk only in open, authorised areas; for swimming, follow local safety instructions and current closures.

overview.title: What You'll See Here
overview.desc: From the "clack-clack" of pebbles to three natural stone arches, Étretat's coastline packages geology with literature, painting, and sea breeze.
overview.cliffs_desc: White chalk cliffs eroded by the sea form natural arches; the most famous are typically called Porte d'Aval / Porte d'Amont.
overview.pebble_desc: The beach is made of pebbles, making walking harder; but that's exactly why it's better to "slow down" and listen to the waves.
overview.tides_desc: Tide times describe sea levels; they never permit entry to closed areas. Follow local signs and closures.
overview.source_info: Information extracted from public sources (Normandy Tourism/Local Tourism Office and Wikipedia), combined with basic info from Google Maps.

tips.title: How to Enjoy It More
tips.desc: Tide times describe sea levels; they never permit entry to closed areas. Follow local signs and closures.
tips.step1_title: First, find your rhythm at the beach
tips.step1_desc: Enjoy the bay from the open promenade. Do not approach the arches over rocks or through tunnels.
tips.step2_desc: Enjoy the bay from the open promenade. Do not approach the arches over rocks or through tunnels.
tips.step3_desc: Stay on marked paths, away from cliff edges and behind barriers. Turn back if conditions or closures require it.
tips.safety_title: Coastal closures also apply at low tide
tips.safety_desc: Municipal order 180/2025 prohibits access to Chambre des demoiselles, the Chaudron descent and tunnels through the cliff headlands. The tourist office also explicitly identifies the Trou à l’Homme cave and tunnel as closed to access. Along the municipal coastline, beach access is prohibited across the full width of the beaches, except in the area directly in front of the seafront promenade. Tide times describe sea levels; they never permit entry to closed areas. Follow local signs and closures.
tips.safety_highlight: Coastal closures also apply at low tide
tips.rule_desc: Pebbles help protect the seafront from waves. Collecting them is prohibited: leave them in place and take a photograph as a souvenir.

map.golden_hour: Parking — Check municipal parking information and signs on arrival; walking times vary.
map.photo_spot: Photos — Use the promenade or authorised viewpoints; never cross a barrier for a photograph.
map.route_plan: Route Planning — Click to plan your route in Google Maps. If driving, be aware that summer weekends can be extremely crowded.
map.parking_tip: Peak hours tip: Park outside the town center and walk in to save time searching for a spot.
map.open_hours_desc: Tide times describe sea levels; they never permit entry to closed areas. Follow local signs and closures.
map.best_light_desc: Sunset hour paints the limestone cliffs in warm amber tones. Arrive 1 hour before sunset.

about.title: About Plage d'Étretat Guide
about.content1: Welcome to the independent guide for Plage d'Étretat! Our mission is to provide comprehensive, objective, and up-to-date information to help you plan your visit to this magnificent natural wonder.
about.content2: We are passionate about Étretat and its unique chalk cliffs, natural arches, and pebble beaches. This website is a labor of love, created by enthusiasts to share the beauty and practical tips for exploring this iconic French destination.
about.content3: Please note that this website is not affiliated with the official management body of Plage d'Étretat. For official information, tickets, or specific regulations, we always recommend consulting official local tourism resources.
